notes: A hub chip means 'every train that calls at filterCrs', fetched server-side via Darwin filterCrs/filterType=to.
absorbs = printed destinations that disappear from the picker because the hub chip covers them.
A printed destination NOT in absorbs keeps its own chip AND its trains also appear under the hub chip.
Hub chips carry no operator suffix — several operators may call at the hub.
v1 scope: Kidderminster only (FB-50). Other West Midlands stations on this corridor (Hagley, Blakedown, Stourbridge Junction, Rowley Regis, etc.) are a proposal for Tim's review, not added here.

London Marylebone (Chiltern Railways) also calls at Snow Hill but is deliberately NOT absorbed — it keeps its own chip; its trains also appear under the Birmingham hub chip. See PR for Tim's confirmation.

hubs.label: Birmingham
hubs.reason: Snow Hill line through-runs past Birmingham onto the Shakespeare Line; riders anchor on Birmingham. BSW not BMO because a Snow Hill-terminating train never calls at Moor Street. Note: the brief's original draft used code "BSH" for Snow Hill, which is actually Bushey (Hertfordshire) in Darwin's CRS scheme — Birmingham Snow Hill's real code is BSW. Corrected here after live-probing on 4 Sep 2026 confirmed BSW returns the full absorbed set at Kidderminster; see PR for the transcript.
